summary: Both filled docs (PartialOrdering.reverse, PartialOrdering.apply) accurately describe their implementations and follow Scaladoc conventions; checked reverse's anonymous-class body (lteq/gteq/lt/gt/equiv/tryCompare all delegate to outer with swapped args) and apply's body (`= ev`) against the prose.

items.issue: The formula `reverse.lteq(x, y) == lteq(y, x)` is mathematically correct (rev.lteq(x,y) == outer.lteq(y,x)) but the unqualified `lteq` could be misread as calling `reverse.lteq` again (self-referential) rather than the receiver's own `lteq`, since `reverse` is named right before it in the same expression.
items.suggestion: Qualify for clarity, e.g. "this.reverse.lteq(x, y) == this.lteq(y, x)" or spell it out in prose ("x and y compare in reverse order").
